01 / The question

How can an agent stay grounded when the work moves beyond the chat?

Why this matters

People work across conversations, documents, and interactive applications. The agent may see the conversation while missing what changed in the workspace. Parallax addresses this grounding asymmetry by connecting task state with application-side evidence.

02 / Contribution & method

My contribution

I translated formative research into the interface and systems for task tracking, semantic read-back, and selective grounding.

Role & scope

I conducted formative user research and translated findings on context loss, workflow continuity, provenance, and user control into design requirements. I designed and implemented task-state tracking, semantic read-back, and selective grounding mechanisms, alongside the interface and backend infrastructure.

01Route the work＋

Route work through a shared task specification

Represent intent, scope, constraints, and required operations. Route work to a specialized application when the conversation lacks the evidence or capability needed to continue.

02Read back evidence＋

Read back meaning with provenance

Transform raw interactions and artifact states into interaction episodes and semantic observations. Preserve the distinction between observed activity, explicit human interpretations, and uncertain agent inferences.

03Ground selectively＋

Ground selectively and explain the choice

Assess evidence relevance, select admissible observations, and check whether the evidence is sufficient. Preserve a trace back to the underlying work, and request clarification or further work when needed.

03 / Evidence

What the work shows

Researchers valued continuity and provenance; deciding when to intervene and how to repair context remained harder.

Team-level findings from small, separate cohorts; no inferential significance tests.

Explore the study & findings

A formative study with five researchers informed the Grounding Loop: Route, Work, Read Back, and Ground. The team then conducted an exploratory evaluation with twelve researchers: eight in Literature Synthesis and four in Network Analysis. Each participant used both a conventional CLI baseline and Parallax, with the same model and task-relevant tools.

Mean System Usability Scale scores were 74.38 for Parallax versus 59.38 for the baseline in Literature Synthesis, and 86.88 versus 47.50 in Network Analysis. Participants valued continuity and provenance, while intervention timing and repair remained less consistent. These are descriptive findings from small, separate cohorts; the paper does not report inferential significance tests.

04 / The next question

How much context should an agent retain—and when should it ask the person to resolve an evidence gap?

A direction to explore

Observable activity does not fully reveal intent: opening a paper may signal uncertainty, and changing a visualization may be exploration rather than commitment. Future work should make grounding repair easier and examine what to capture, retain, or exclude across longer workflows and more applications.
